query: How does my sleep compare to similar profiles?
reply:
Your 30-day sleep average of 7.1 hours is in the healthy range — 60% of US adults land between 7 and 9 hours.

Compared to the reference cohort: you're sleeping slightly less than the casual runner [1] (7.4h) and the CrossFit regular [2] (7.6h), both of whom protect consistent bedtimes as part of their training routines. The yoga + hiking persona [3] (7.5h) is your closest match — similar activity level, similar sleep. The new parent [4] (5.7h) is significantly below you; his fragmented sleep pattern is common in early parenthood and falls in the short-sleep band where about 29% of men 18-44 land.

Your minimum of 5.8h suggests some nights are still short. The 2.6-hour gap between your best (8.4h) and worst nights is worth watching — if the short nights cluster around specific days, that's a pattern you could act on.

This is decision-support context, not medical advice. If sleep quality feels poor despite adequate duration, that's worth raising with a clinician.

contributors.label: casual runner, F, age 25-29
contributors.narrative_summary: Logs 3 weekday morning runs of 30-45 minutes plus a weekend long run. Sleep is decent because she protects an 11pm bedtime.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within trained-recreational range; avram_2019 reports women 18-44 middle 50% spans roughly 62-78 bpm with lower values among regular exercisers.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'somewhat active' band (7500-9999); higher end consistent with sub-elite runner.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhanes_2007_2010_sleep 7-9h healthy range (60.4% of adults).
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min moderate threshold; within 150-300 recommended range.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Meets aerobic frequency expected for cdc_pa_2024 guideline-meeters.

contributors.label: CrossFit regular, F, age 28-33
contributors.narrative_summary: Five class sessions weekly mixing strength, conditioning, and Olympic lifts. Adds easy zone-2 cardio on rest days for recovery.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Lower bound of reimers_2018 trained-recreational range; appropriate for HIIT/strength-trained female.
source_notes.steps_daily_avg: tudor_locke_2011 'somewhat active'; CrossFit doesn't generate huge step counts but lifestyle is active.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhanes_2007_2010_sleep healthy range; serious recreational athletes often prioritize sleep.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Exceeds cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-300 min range; supports high-volume training.

contributors.label: yoga + hiking, F, age 45-52
contributors.narrative_summary: Three yoga classes plus 1-2 longer hikes weekly. Lifts light weights twice a week. Sleep is consistent thanks to a stable bedtime.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Within avram_2019 active-female-midlife range; moderate aerobic conditioning.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep healthy range; women 45-64 30.7% <7h, so this persona is in the 69% who meet guideline.

contributors.label: new parent, low sleep, M, age 30-34
contributors.narrative_summary: Activity dropped after his second kid. Sleep is fragmented across nights — total time in bed is fine but consolidated sleep is short.

source_notes.resting_hr_bpm: Matches ostchega_2011 NHANES adult mean (72 bpm); typical for moderately-active middle-young male.
source_notes.sleep_hours_avg: Within nhis_2020_sleep short-sleep band; 28.8% of men 18-44 report <7h, sleep fragmentation common in early parenthood.
source_notes.active_minutes_weekly: Below cdc_pa_guidelines_2018 150-min threshold; consistent with reduced volume in parenting years.
source_notes.workout_sessions_weekly: Partial adherence to aerobic guideline; no muscle-strengthening compliance.

references_used.avram_2019: Avram R, Tison GH, Aschbacher K, et al. Real-world heart rate norms in the Health eHeart study. NPJ Digit Med. 2019;2:58. doi:10.1038/s41746-019-0134-9. n=92,457 US adults; mean real-world HR 79.1 ± 14.5 bpm; women ~4 bpm higher than men.
references_used.tudor_locke_2011: Tudor-Locke C, Craig CL, Brown WJ, et al. How many steps/day are enough? For adults. Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act. 2011;8:79. Step-defined zones: <5000 sedentary, 5000-7499 low active, 7500-9999 somewhat active, 10000-12499 active, ≥12500 highly active.
references_used.nhanes_2007_2010_sleep: Frenk SM, Chong Y. QuickStats: Sleep duration among adults aged ≥20 years, by race/ethnicity — NHANES 2007-2010. MMWR. 2013. 60.4% slept 7-9h; 37.3% slept ≤6h; 2.3% slept ≥10h.
references_used.nhis_2020_sleep: Adjaye-Gbewonyo D, Ng AE, Black LI. QuickStats: Percentage of adults aged ≥18 years who sleep <7 hours, by sex and age group — NHIS 2020. MMWR Morb Mortal Wkly Rep. 2022;71(10):393.
references_used.reimers_2018: Reimers AK, Knapp G, Reimers CD. Effects of exercise on the resting heart rate: A systematic review and meta-analysis of interventional studies. J Clin Med. 2018;7(12):503. PMC6306777.
references_used.cdc_pa_guidelines_2018: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition. 2018.
references_used.cdc_pa_2024: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. National Health Interview Survey 2024. 47.2% of US adults met the aerobic physical activity guideline.
references_used.ostchega_2011: Ostchega Y, Porter KS, Hughes J, Dillon CF, Nwankwo T. Resting pulse rate reference data for children, adolescents, and adults: United States, 1999-2008. Natl Health Stat Report. 2011;(41):1-16.
